extracted.intended_audience: small_businesses and research institutions preparing SBIR/STTR Phase II (NIH/NIAID) applications
extracted.subtask_description: Writing the Commercialization Plan and Budget Justification for an NIH/NIAID STTR Phase II application, including required eligibility questions, budget details, team roles, product target profiles, IND-enabling studies, regulatory pathway, and commercialization milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior/Key Personnel (roles, effort, responsibilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior/Key Personnel entries (example: Ronald Harty, PhD, PI (25% effort – 3.0 ca mo)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each senior/key person provide name, degree/title, percent effort (calendar or academic months), a short bio/qualifications, explicit responsibilities on the project (e.g., direct studies to test lead compounds, direct communication/joint lab meetings), and their role in project oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Personnel (research staff roles and effort)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other Personnel entries (example: Research Specialist Ziying Han, MD, Ph.D. (100% effort – 12.0 ca mo)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe duties (e.g., maintain tissue culture models, perform molecular biology techniques, maintain supplies), percent effort, and justification of why the personnel are needed based on preliminary data and the proposed tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials, supplies, and core facility fees justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials and supplies requested to cover cell culture, molecular virology, antibodies, imaging assays, reagents, and costs associated with University core facilities (e.g., Leica SP5 confocal systems).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe specific categories of consumables and reagents, any facility fee policy (who is charged and fee rationale), and include estimated costs and purpose (e.g., imaging core hourly fee to defray maintenance and operation costs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe benefits (use negotiated rates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fringe benefits requested for salaries in this budget at the DHHS negotiated rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the applicable negotiated fringe benefit rate (example in text: 29.5% or Texas Biomed 29.51%) and apply consistently to salary lines; cite negotiated agreement if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect costs / F&A (apply negotiated/modified direct cost rates)
rubrics_metrics.description: A total modified direct cost rate has been requested; examples: DHHS negotiated rate 62% (then 62.5% from specified date); Texas Biomed Federal MTDC Rate 98%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the applicant or subawardee's federally negotiated indirect cost rate and specify effective dates; indicate whether consortium/contractual F&A is excluded when determining direct cost limits per NIH policy (NOT-OD-05-004).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget justification for in vivo animal studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget line-items and justification for in vivo toxicity, accumulation, and ABSL4 efficacy studies including numbers of animals, purchase/shipment, housing fees, dosing, necropsy, pathology, histopathology, required supplies, reagents, and veterinary personnel effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit animal counts, sex, ages (example: 4-5-week old BALB/c mice), breakdown of costs (purchase, housing, dosing, necropsy, histopathology), and justification tying study design to the project aims and regulatory needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR mandatory application and eligibility questions (Questions 1–7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Required SBIR/STTR application questions: organization eligible as a small business at time of award; anticipated number of personnel at award; ownership by venture capital/PE/hedge funds; faculty- or student-owned status; subcontracts with federal labs; HUBZone status; whether all R&D will be performed entirely in the U.S.; prior proposals/awards for essentially equivalent work; disclosure permission; requirement to include a Commercialization Plan where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete and truthfully answer all required checkbox questions; provide explanations and attachments where the form requests (e.g., explanation for R&D partly outside U.S., Commercialization Plan file).

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR-specific and STTR-specific eligibility items (Questions 8–12)
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR-only items (Phase history, PI primary employment), and STTR-only items (PD/PI formal appointment/commitment and ≥10% effort; small business performs ≥40% and research institution ≥30% of the work; DUNS number of nonprofit research partner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For STTR ensure PD/PI has the required formal appointment/commitment and percent effort; document the percent of work split between small business and research institution; include required identifiers (DUNS) and attachments (commercialization history if asked).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization Plan required topics and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercialization Plan should cover value of the project, expected outcomes and impact, key technology objectives, therapeutic benefit, commercial need, competitive advantage versus standard of care, and a path to commercialization including timelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow agency-specific instructions for Commercialization Plan content; include market/need analysis, competitive landscape, routes to market, milestones, and resources required. The application referenced follows STTR guidelines and includes a Technology Niche Analysis as supporting material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target product profile / desired preclinical drug candidate attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: By the end of Phase II the candidate(s) should be: potent orally available inhibitors of RNA virus egress (IC50 <100 nM for example), broad spectrum against RNA viruses, non-cytotoxic at ≥20× live virus IC50, suitable ADME/PK for once-daily oral dosing in mice, demonstrate oral activity in mouse antiviral assay, minimal cytochrome P450 inhibitory activity across key isoforms, minimal hERG activity in patch clamp, minimal Ames mutagenicity, efficient and scalable chemical syntheses, and provide basis for composition-of-matter U.S. patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define quantitative targets where possible (e.g., IC50 thresholds, cytotoxicity margins), include ADME/PK benchmarks, and ensure candidate profiles support IND enabling studies and IP filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: IND-enabling studies and GLP requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Planned IND enabling activities: produce non-GMP and GMP batches (e.g., 300 g non-GMP; prepare 5 kg GMP API later), selection of salt/formulation/crystallinity assessment, analytical methods development, drug substance stability testing, metabolite identification (human, rat, monkey), full PK in three safety species (mouse, rabbit, NHP), Cyp450 inhibition/induction and transporter studies, GLP in vitro toxicology (hERG, Ames, genotoxicity), dose-ranging and 28-day safety in mice and NHPs, safety pharmacology studies (cardiovascular in dogs, CNS/respiratory in rats as needed), reproductive toxicology, GLP placebo-controlled animal efficacy studies under the Animal Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan and budget for GLP-compliant toxicity and pharmacology studies, choose appropriate species for PK/Tox, and coordinate pre-IND discussions with FDA to confirm study design and endpoints; document timelines and go/no-go criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory pathway: Animal Rule (21 CFR Part 314 Subpart 1) when human efficacy trials are impracticable
rubrics_metrics.description: If human clinical trials cannot ethically or feasibly determine effectiveness (e.g., primary indication Marburg), the regulatory pathway may rely on the FDA 'Animal Rule' for approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design pivotal animal efficacy studies in accordance with the Animal Rule expectations (two or more adequate and well-controlled animal models predictive for humans), include survival and viral load endpoints, and consult FDA via pre-IND to align on study design.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPLT / Project governance and advisory structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a Project Leadership Team (PPLT) to interpret data and provide strategic direction, with regular (at least monthly) advice and formal quarterly meetings chaired by the PI; PPLT members may add agenda items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define membership (internal PI, company leadership, external advisors), roles (data interpretation, experimental design coordination, strategic decisions), meeting frequency, and decision processes to ensure rapid iterative development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization milestones and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Planned milestones include pre-IND meeting with FDA prior to IND-enabling studies, target IND filing (~2Q/2024 in text), First-in-Human dosing (~1Q/2025), and Phase I design (single/multiple ascending dose, ~12 months, ~40 subjects, ~$3M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a realistic timeline for CMC, IND-enabling studies, regulatory interactions, IND submission, and first-in-human studies; include assumptions, dependencies (e.g., partnering), and contingency plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficacy endpoints for pivotal animal studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Pivotal efficacy studies should show enhanced survival in two or more GLP double-blind placebo-controlled animal models of Ebola (or relevant virus), and assess viral load and survival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify models, primary and secondary endpoints (survival, viral load), study design (blinding, controls), statistical power, and GLP compliance to support Animal Rule efficacy claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMC / manufacturing and formulation activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Planned CMC tasks: prepare 300 g non-GMP API, select salt form, vehicle and formulation, evaluate crystallinity and polymorph propensity, analytical methods development, stability testing, and later prepare 5 kg GMP API.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document batch sizes, process scalability, formulation rationale, analytical method validation needs, stability protocol (shelf-life and stress testing), and budget/time estimates to support IND chemistry requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property and patenting strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the basis for one or more composition of matter U.S. patent applications and plan to file additional provisional and PCT patent applications as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe freedom-to-operate considerations, timing of filings relative to public disclosure and development milestones, and allocation of IP responsibilities between small business and research partner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of subcontract and consortium F&A exclusions for direct cost limits
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH policy (NOT-OD-05-004) allows applicants to exclude consortium/contractual F&A costs when determining whether an application falls beneath any applicable direct cost limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a direct cost limit is specified in an FOA, compute Total Direct Costs less Consortium F&A per NIH table guidance to demonstrate compliance with any direct cost caps.
